subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Nylon-6,6 is a polyamide formed by condensation of which monomers?
options: A diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
A diol and a dicarboxylic acid
questions.explain: Nylon-6,6 forms from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid joined by amide links with loss of water.

questions.q: Benzene is more stable than the hypothetical Kekule cyclohexa-1,3,5-triene because of what?
options: Delocalisation of pi electrons over the ring
questions.explain: The six pi electrons are delocalised above and below the ring, giving extra (resonance) stabilisation.

questions.q: Reaction of an acid anhydride such as ethanoic anhydride with an alcohol produces which products?
options: An ester and a carboxylic acid
questions.explain: An acid anhydride reacts with an alcohol to give an ester plus a carboxylic acid.

questions.q: In strongly acidic solution, an amino acid such as glycine exists mainly as which ion?
questions.explain: In low pH the carboxylate is protonated and the amine is protonated, giving an overall positive cation.

questions.q: For a weak acid HA, the acid dissociation constant Ka is given by:
questions.explain: Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA] for the equilibrium HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻.

questions.q: Which reagent converts a carboxylic acid into an acyl chloride?
questions.explain: Thionyl chloride converts the carboxylic acid into the acyl chloride, with SO2 and HCl as by-products.

questions.q: Why are aromatic amines such as phenylamine weaker bases than aliphatic amines?
options: They form hydrogen bonds with water
The nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring
questions.explain: In phenylamine the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the ring, making it less available to accept a proton.

questions.q: Reduction of propanone with NaBH4 gives which product?
questions.explain: NaBH4 reduces the ketone propanone to the secondary alcohol propan-2-ol.

questions.q: What is the pH of a solution with [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³?
For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing the temperature will:
options: leave Kc unchanged but shift left
decrease Kc and shift equilibrium left
increase Kc and shift equilibrium right
questions.explain: Raising temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, decreasing Kc and shifting equilibrium towards reactants.

questions.q: An acidic buffer is typically made from:
options: a weak acid and its salt (conjugate base)
a weak base and a strong acid
a strong acid and its salt
questions.explain: An acidic buffer contains a weak acid plus its conjugate base (e.g. CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻).

questions.q: For the reaction 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), increasing pressure at constant temperature shifts the equilibrium:
questions.explain: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (1 mol N₂O₄ vs 2 mol NO₂), shifting right.

questions.q: Which reagents are used to prepare an ester from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol?
questions.explain: Esterification is catalysed by concentrated sulfuric acid, with the acid and alcohol warmed together.

questions.q: In a Friedel-Crafts acylation, what is the role of the AlCl3 catalyst?
options: It acts as a halogen carrier generating the acylium electrophile
questions.explain: AlCl3 polarises the acyl chloride to generate the electrophilic acylium ion that attacks benzene.

questions.q: A polyester such as Terylene is formed by condensation between which monomers?
options: A diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
A diol and a dicarboxylic acid
questions.explain: Polyesters form by condensation of a diol with a dicarboxylic acid (or diacyl chloride), losing water.

questions.q: Benzene typically reacts with electrophiles by which mechanism?
questions.explain: Substitution preserves the stable delocalised ring, so benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution rather than addition.

questions.q: Which reagent reduces a carboxylic acid such as ethanoic acid to a primary alcohol?
questions.explain: LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent that reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols.

questions.q: What is the pH of 0.050 mol dm⁻³ NaOH at 25 °C? (log 5 ≈ 0.70)
Why do ketones give a negative result with Tollens' and Fehling's reagents?
options: They are already fully oxidised acids
They cannot be oxidised easily as there is no H on the carbonyl carbon
questions.explain: Ketones have no hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon, so they resist the mild oxidation these reagents provide.

questions.q: A buffer solution is one that:
options: resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or alkali are added
questions.explain: A buffer minimises (resists) pH change on addition of small amounts of acid or base, not preventing it entirely.

questions.q: In an ethanoic acid/ethanoate buffer, when a small amount of acid (H⁺) is added it is removed by reaction with:
questions.explain: Added H⁺ reacts with the conjugate base CH₃COO⁻ to form CH₃COOH, limiting the pH change.

questions.q: Which type of linkage joins amino acids in a protein?
questions.explain: Amino acids condense to form amide bonds, known as peptide links, releasing water.

questions.q: Why is ethylamine a stronger base than ammonia?
options: The ethyl group withdraws electron density
The ethyl group is electron-donating, increasing electron density on N
It has a smaller lone pair
questions.explain: The electron-donating alkyl group increases electron density on the nitrogen, making the lone pair more available.

questions.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.10 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak acid with Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ (assume [H⁺] = √(Ka × c)).
Acyl chlorides react with alcohols to form which class of compound?
questions.explain: An acyl chloride reacts vigorously with an alcohol to form an ester, releasing HCl.

questions.q: Acid hydrolysis of an ester such as ethyl ethanoate produces which two products?
options: A carboxylate salt and an alcohol
A carboxylic acid and an alcohol
questions.explain: Acidic hydrolysis reverses esterification to give the carboxylic acid and the alcohol.

questions.q: Hydrolysis of a nitrile RCN under acidic conditions gives which product?
questions.explain: Acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile yields the corresponding carboxylic acid (plus ammonium ions).

questions.q: A strong monobasic acid differs from a weak monobasic acid because the strong acid:
options: has a larger Ka but does not fully dissociate
questions.explain: A strong acid is, by definition, fully (essentially completely) dissociated in aqueous solution.

questions.q: What is observed when an aldehyde is warmed with Fehling's solution?
options: A brick-red precipitate of Cu2O forms
questions.explain: Aldehydes reduce the blue Cu2+ complex in Fehling's to a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide.

questions.q: What are the units of Kc for the reaction H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)?
questions.explain: With equal moles of gas on both sides the concentration terms cancel, so Kc is dimensionless.
